The AM1 superalloy is a second-generation nickel-based single crystal alloy with a nominal composition of Ni-5Co-3Cr-12.5Al-2.5W-2Ta-0.4Mo-1.2Ti (atomic %).
The γ and γ' phases in the AM1 superalloy are coherent, with the γ' phase making up about 70% of the total volume at room temperature.
The misfit between the γ and γ' phases is negative and equal to -10^-3 at 950°C.
Repeated fatigue tests (R=0) were performed at 950°C with a frequency of 0.25 Hz, varying the number of cycles (N) from 1 to 20,000 and the total strain amplitude (εt) from 1.6% to 2.2%.
Two main types of deformation microstructures were observed: anisotropic microstructures (domain A) and homogeneous microstructures (domain H).
The anisotropy in the deformation microstructure is due to a partition of plasticity in the γ channels or oriented coarsening of the γ' precipitates.
As the number of cycles increases, the deformation spreads from the horizontal channels perpendicular to the loading axis to the vertical channels parallel to the loading axis.
The negative misfit between the γ and γ' phases leads to compressive internal stresses in the vertical channels, making the horizontal channels easier to deform initially.
Only 4-6 dislocations at the γ/γ' interfaces are needed to fully relax the misfit on the {001} interfaces.
At high total strain amplitudes (εt=2.2%), significant shearing of the γ' precipitates is observed, reducing the anisotropy of the deformation microstructure.

Alternate fatigue (R=-1) leads to a microstructure that is a combination of the microstructures observed under simple tension and simple compression, with shearing of the γ' precipitates and the formation of extrinsic stacking faults.
Véron's model explains the type N coarsening of the γ' precipitates under repeated fatigue as a consequence of the anisotropy and nature of the deformation at the precipitate scale.

At lower temperatures, precipitate shearing is expected to be more significant, while at higher temperatures, diffusion processes would be stronger, leading to easier dislocation climb and a shift of the homogeneous deformation domain.
Under simple compression, the dislocations are primarily located in the {010} and {100} channels, in contrast to the simple tension case where they are mainly at the {001} interfaces.
The critical number of cycles (No) at which the misfit is effectively relaxed is estimated to be in the range of 1 to 25 cycles, depending on the total strain amplitude.
